# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the position described in discovery.

The Client runs three AI use cases, each at a different stage:

* A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal.
* AI visual inspection is in pilot on the German production line.
* AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. These give it established disciplines for document control, internal audit and management review that AI governance can build on rather than duplicate.

In June 2026 an internal audit found that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. That finding is the most immediate gap. Without an inventory, the Client cannot reliably classify use cases, assign accountable owners or show which systems fall within scope of the EU AI Act and GDPR.

Your stated objective is clear: governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, but the start date is not fixed. Three further constraints shape this proposal:

* Customer data must remain in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
* Approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. Why Continuous Fractional Advisory at This Stage

At the Piloting stage of AI maturity, governance decisions are being made in real time, often by different functions. Quality, Security, Data, the German plant and Legal each hold part of the picture. A one-off assessment would describe the gap but would not help these functions make consistent decisions as the visual inspection pilot moves toward production and sales forecasting moves toward build.

A fractional advisor provides senior governance judgment on a steady rhythm. It keeps the Q2 2027 production milestone and later ISO/IEC 42001 readiness on one coordinated path, and it lets your existing internal auditors and management system owners carry the work forward.

The engagement is grounded in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, this means production decisions about visual inspection stay with named Tamarack leaders, and every recommendation is documented so those leaders can decide with full information.

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement start date is Unknown and will be fixed at contract. The quarters below are engagement quarters. If the engagement begins in January 2027, Quarter 2 coincides with the Q2 2027 production window. For that reason, governance for visual inspection is front-loaded into Quarter 1.

**Quarter 1: Establish.** This quarter closes the June 2026 audit finding and sets the foundations:

* Build the AI system inventory, starting with the chatbot, the inspection pilot and the forecasting plan.
* Draft the AI policy and define accountable owners across Legal, Security, Quality, Data and the German plant.
* Run a structured risk assessment of the visual inspection pilot.
* Prepare a preliminary EU AI Act classification view of each use case and a GDPR data flow review. Both are flagged for verification by external counsel, and neither is presented as settled advice.
* Help the German plant manager prepare clear materials for works council consultation. Labor law questions route to counsel.

**Quarter 2: Production Readiness.** This quarter prepares the go/no-go decision for visual inspection:

* Define a production readiness gate for visual inspection, including human oversight, performance monitoring, fallback procedures and evidence of works council consultation.
* Embed that gate in existing ISO 9001 change control.
* Review the chatbot for EU data residency and for disclosure to customers that they are interacting with AI. Any regulatory interpretation is flagged for counsel verification.

**Quarter 3: Integrate.** This quarter folds AI governance into the systems Tamarack already runs:

* Integrate AI governance controls into the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 management systems.
* Run sales forecasting through the new intake and risk process before build begins.
* Equip the two internal auditors to audit AI governance controls using the GRC Workbook.

**Quarter 4: Assure.** This quarter builds ISO/IEC 42001 readiness:

* Complete a gap assessment against ISO/IEC 42001.
* Draft the Statement of Applicability.
* Run an internal audit rehearsal and prepare management review inputs.

The ISO/IEC 42001 start date and any external certification audit date are Unknown and flagged for intake. If the start date is set earlier, audit preparation work moves forward accordingly. This work builds readiness only. Certification outcomes are determined solely by the Client's chosen certification body and are not promised.

## 4. Cadence and Access

The engagement runs on four channels:

* **Monthly executive advisory session** with you and the executives you nominate.
* **Monthly working session** with the governance team: the CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and internal auditors.
* **Asynchronous availability** for defined question categories, with response windows agreed in Month 1.
* **Quarterly governance review** to measure progress against this arc.

The working method draws on two frameworks:

* **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for controls, risk and evidence.
* **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for deliberate use case intake and design.

Board-level reporting can draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. All legal questions, including EU AI Act, GDPR and works council matters, route to external counsel.

## 6. Investment

The fee is **US$10,000 per month** for twelve months, renewable. The total twelve-month fee is US$120,000.

Your approved budget for this fiscal year is up to US$80,000, which covers up to eight monthly fees. The fiscal year end date and the engagement start date are both Unknown, so the portion of the engagement that falls within the current fiscal year cannot yet be confirmed. Please confirm both dates so we can show exactly which months fall into the following fiscal year and will need approval there.
